body: Metal Warriors is LucasArts' Super Nintendo action game about Lieutenant Stone piloting combat suits against the Dark Axis. The side-scrolling missions combine shooting with exploration, and several different machines can be used during the same operation. The pilot can leave one suit and search for another, turning a robot into a piece of equipment rather than a permanent identity. A vehicle that initially looks like the player's character becomes one possible answer to the terrain and enemies waiting in the next part of the mission.

Six suit types have different weapons and movement characteristics. An agile machine, a heavily armed walker and a specialised climbing unit give the same environment different possibilities. Power-ups can add weapons and restore damage, while taking enough punishment can disable useful equipment. The choice of machine affects how a route can be crossed as much as how an enemy is attacked. Leaving a damaged suit creates a vulnerable interval for the pilot, making the search for a replacement part of the mission's tension.

Designers Mike Ebert and Dean Sharpe brought experience from Zombies Ate My Neighbors, with the project using an improved version of that game's engine. Konami published Metal Warriors in North America in 1995. A two-player competitive mode lets the machines and their differences meet directly outside the campaign. Its defining idea remains the relationship between pilot and suit: a formidable body can be abandoned, taken over or replaced, so recognising the next useful machine is as important as firing the weapon already in hand.
